title: UrbanLake
summary: Make NYC service-request history reproducible, queryable and useful for demand forecasting.
problem: City service data changes over time. A useful forecasting platform needs reconciled history, data-quality checks and evaluation that respects time.
approach: Built bounded API ingestion, Kafka replay and Bronze / Silver / Gold Delta processing. Source polling reconciles observations; it is not CDC.
Implemented shifted lag features, a seasonal-naive baseline and chronological validation/test periods.
Separated a lightweight hosted analytics release from the local full-data pipeline and operational services.
outcome: The recorded November 4 run reconciled 23,008,706 requests. Its historical random forest MAE was 788.40 requests/day versus 1,089.72 for lag-seven on 497 test days. This audit inspected source and the run ledger; it did not reproduce the full data run.
scope: Historical one-day-ahead backtest with observed lags. Source revisions limit point-in-time validity. Snapshot ends November 1, 2026; this is not a current forecast service.

title: KnowDoc AI
summary: Ask questions of private documents and inspect the exact source passage, version and page.
problem: Document answers need traceable evidence and permission boundaries, especially when documents are shared, revised or revoked.
approach: Implemented ingestion, checksummed versions, access-aware retrieval and citation resolution.
Built local keyword, dense, hybrid and optional reranked retrieval with Ollama generation.
Published a constrained hosted edition: PostgreSQL keyword retrieval, supported profile extraction and source passages; general generation is disabled.
outcome: The developer-authored local benchmark compares 45 retrieval cases and 80 behavior cases. Hybrid with reranking recorded Recall@5 of 0.911; plain hybrid underperformed dense retrieval. Human semantic grading remains open, and recorded generation/injection failures are retained.
scope: Hosted demo does not offer hybrid retrieval, reranking or general generative answering. Citation integrity is not semantic correctness. Exploratory benchmark annotations lack independent review.

title: CareFlow AI
summary: Investigate hospital admission outcomes with reproducible features and hospital-grouped evaluation.
problem: Retrospective admission modeling requires clear target definitions and evaluation that reduces leakage across hospitals.
approach: Prepared CDC NHAMCS emergency department data with explicit admission targets and feature processing.
Implemented two GroupShuffleSplit stages and assertions that hospitals never cross train, validation and test partitions.
Connected an XGBoost pipeline and SHAP analysis to a local FastAPI service and React research dashboard.
outcome: Training code evaluates training and validation partitions while preserving the held-out test partition. No final test or clinical performance claim is made.
scope: Educational retrospective research only. Not clinically validated; never use for admission, discharge, treatment or other clinical decisions. Public deployment and held-out evaluation are pending.

title: CollabDocs
summary: Draft, import and share rich-text documents with persistence and explicit conflict handling.
problem: A shared document workspace needs durable content, owner/editor permissions and protection against silent stale-write overwrites.
approach: Implemented rich-text JSON persistence, autosave, TXT/Markdown import and owner/editor sharing.
Added conditional version checks to reject stale saves and owner-only document deletion.
Built and documented the application as a time-constrained assessment with selectable Alice/Bob demo identities.
outcome: Source includes domain and delete-route tests plus browser coverage for owner-only deletion. Existing release records report 17 unit tests. This is not real-time collaborative merging.
scope: Assessment demo: anyone can select either identity. No secure authentication, sharing revocation or document version history. Use synthetic sample content only.

title: Diamonds analytics
summary: Explore how carat, cut and color relate to diamond pricing through an interactive Power BI report.
problem: Multivariate pricing data is easier to explore through linked views than a raw spreadsheet.
approach: Created a Power BI report with pricing, carat, color and cut views.
Published the PBIX, CSV, workflow and dashboard preview for inspection.
Kept this descriptive analytics work separate from causal pricing or predictive-model claims.
outcome: Repository includes the report, source CSV, static PDF and screenshot. Power BI Desktop is required for interactive exploration; no hosted Power BI Service deployment is claimed.
scope: Supporting analytics project. Dataset origin/license and a reproducible measure dictionary need stronger documentation. This audit did not execute the PBIX.
